AUTHOR: Zouin
TITLE: Improving CNN Fish Detection and Classification with Tracking
REGION: Deep slopes and seamounts, New Caledonia, South Pacific
SPECIES: Deepwater snappers (Lutjanidae): Pristipomoides filamentosus, P. flavipinnis, P. argyrogrammicus, Aphareus rutilans, Aprion virescens, Etelis coruscans, Parapristipomoides squamimaxillaris
DATA: Own deep BRUVS GoPro footage: 289 15-s videos (159 train, 130 test); 3521 training images at 1 fps
V_EV: Sec. 2: 'a 1200 lumens, 120-degree angle led light ... recorded at depths varying between 47 and 552 m'
D_EV: Sec. 2: 'split into a training set of 159 ... videos ... and a testing dataset made of 130 videos ... ensured that the testing and training datasets were independent'
R_EV: Sec. 2: test set of 130 videos drawn from the same New Caledonia deep BRUVS video dataset as training
C_EV: Sec. 3.7: 'we perform a post-processing step to eliminate potentially erroneous IDs ... If two bounding boxes exhibit a significant overlap ... likely to correspond to the same object'; Appendix A 'Detection Threshold: 0.5'
E_EV: Sec. 3.8: 'To evaluate the accuracy of our algorithm, we calculated F1-Scores for each species.'
ARCH: Faster R-CNN Inception-ResNet V2 + OpenCV legacy tracker (forward/backward) + IoU-based ID post-processing
METR: Per-species precision, recall, F1, detection accuracy, processing time
NOTE: Video-level split explicitly to ensure independence (D4=Y). Test only on same campaign dataset -> R1=N. C5 coded 중복계수 처리: post-processing merges overlapping IDs and uses majority class per track; detection threshold 0.5 fixed (C1=Y) -> C_ALL Y by rule even though no threshold sweep. '12% more individuals' refers to box-level detection gain; no ecological count/MaxN comparison, so E1=없음. Turbidity mentioned only as general limitation.
